bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the MemorySanitizer crash against the exact staged zlib checkout `e4dd1d93ae60fb0a14f0cf3d7c54e767ba1663fe`. The exact staged witness is 538 bytes with first byte `0xe0`. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`, the harness stores the buffer and size in globals and derives `dictionaryLen = 224` from that first byte. In `test_dict_deflate()`, the same byte yields `level = 3`, raw `windowBits = 8`, `memLevel = 9`, and `strategy = 4`. `deflateInit2_()` promotes `windowBits` to 9, allocates `s->prev[512]` with malloc-backed `ZALLOC`, and stores `s->level = 3` plus `s->strategy = 4` in the deflate state. `lm_init()` clears only `head[]`, leaves `prev[]` intentionally uninitialized, and derives `s->max_lazy_match` from `configuration_table[3].max_lazy = 6`, which `deflate_fast` later uses as `max_insert_length`. `deflateSetDictionary()` preloads the first 224 bytes of the same witness, initializes dictionary positions `0..221`, and leaves `strstart = 224` with `insert = 2`; the first `fill_window()` during real compression immediately consumes that carry-over state and initializes positions `222` and `223`. `deflate()` then dispatches to `deflate_fast` because `s->level != 0`, `s->strategy` is neither `Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY` nor `Z_RLE`, and `configuration_table[3].func` is `deflate_fast`. On this level-3 fast path, any later match longer than `max_insert_length == 6` advances `strstart` without `INSERT_STRING` on the skipped positions, so later `prev[]` entries can remain untouched while input is consumed. Because `224 + 538 = 762`, `fill_window()` eventually reaches `strstart >= wsize + MAX_DIST(s)` with `wsize = 512` and `MAX_DIST = 250`, calls `slide_hash()`, and that loop reads `m = *--p` from a `prev[]` entry that is still garbage. The next line uses `m` in `m >= wsize ? m - wsize : NIL`, producing the saved `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/zlib/deflate.c:222:20`. The staged fix does not initialize `prev[]`; it suppresses this known MSAN report by marking `slide_hash()` `no_sanitize("memory")`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled input and creates the deflate parameter tuple later copied into `s->level` and `s->strategy`, used to size the state, and used to select the `deflate_fast` path plus its `max_insert_length`.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer entry point first stores the exact staged 538-byte witness (sha256 `386e8e62c47580703ab0972569c39baa2b587c0edf64743ff5ed6c79c89ce87a`) into global `data` and `dataLen` at `/src/example_dict_fuzzer.c:146-147`, then derives `dictionaryLen = 224` from `data[0]` at lines 152-154. When `test_dict_deflate()` reaches this statement, the same witness byte `data[0] == 0xe0` yields `level = 3`, raw `windowBits = 8`, `memLevel = 9`, and `strategy = 4`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state is the contents of `s->prev`. This allocation creates the 512-entry hash-chain array that later supplies the poisoned `prev[n]` value read in `slide_hash()`. On this platform `ZALLOC` ultimately uses malloc-backed `zcalloc()` rather than zeroing the buffer.

root_cause.description: The source-level defect is that `slide_hash()` reads `s->prev[n]` into `m` even though initialization explicitly covers only inserted positions (`0..221` from the dictionary plus `222..223` from the carry-over loop) and later fast-compression matches can skip inserting intermediate positions entirely.
root_cause.note: The adjacent comment at lines 223-224 explicitly acknowledges that `prev[n]` may be garbage when `n` is not on any hash chain. The staged fix does not initialize `prev[]`; it suppresses MemorySanitizer for the whole function instead.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The ternary's `m >= wsize` comparison consumes the uninitialized `m` loaded in the previous step while rewriting the slid hash entry.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/zlib/deflate.c:222:20` in `slide_hash` with stack `slide_hash -> fill_window -> deflate_fast -> deflate -> test_dict_deflate`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 538-byte witness passes the fuzz target's only size gate and is forwarded into `test_dict_deflate()`.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is workspace checkout `e4dd1d93ae60fb0a14f0cf3d7c54e767ba1663fe`, not metadata commit `1411ccafc0f50997b56135c3ee542fdfe9d7f34c`.

The saved traces and staged source prove that `slide_hash()` read a later `s->prev[n]` slot left untouched after the dictionary inserts and carry-over inserts `222`/`223`, but they do not identify the exact modulo-512 index `n` or the exact long-match sequence in `deflate_fast()` that skipped its insertion.
Stage 02 did not run a fixed build. `patch_resolves` below is source-grounded from the staged diff, which suppresses MSAN in `slide_hash()` rather than initializing `s->prev`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness stores the witness buffer and length in globals, derives `dictionaryLen = 224` from the first byte `0xe0`, and passes that state into the helper.
The helper decodes the same witness byte into the deflate parameter tuple and later uses the witness as both preset dictionary and compression input.
zlib promotes the raw 8-bit window to 9 bits, allocates `s->prev[512]` with malloc-backed `ZALLOC`, and stores `level = 3` / `strategy = 4` into the deflate state.
State reset clears only `head[]`, leaves `prev[]` to be initialized on demand, and derives the level-3 `max_lazy_match` / `max_insert_length = 6` limit from `configuration_table[3]`.
The 224-byte preset dictionary initializes positions `0..221` and then leaves `strstart = 224` with `insert = 2`.
The real compression call dispatches to `deflate_fast` because the stored state is level 3 and strategy 4.
The first `fill_window()` of real compression consumes `insert = 2` and initializes carry-over positions `222` and `223`.

While consuming the full 538-byte witness, the level-3 fast path can skip `INSERT_STRING` on later long matches, allowing at least one later `prev[]` slot to remain untouched as `strstart` advances toward the slide threshold.
Once `fill_window()` reaches the exact slide threshold, `slide_hash()` reads an untouched `prev[]` slot into `m`, and the following comparison on `m` triggers the saved MSAN report.

fine_trace.note: The harness stores the exact fuzz buffer and byte length in globals consumed later by both `deflateSetDictionary()` and `deflate()`. For the staged PoC this materializes `data = d` and `dataLen = 538`.
The first witness byte is read through the new global alias and copied into `dictionaryLen`. With `data[0] == 0xe0`, the preset-dictionary length becomes 224.
The length clamp is evaluated before compression starts. Because `dictionaryLen == 224` and `dataLen == 538`, the branch is not taken and the later dictionary preload still uses 224 bytes.

First non-harness consumption of attacker input on the vulnerable path. The same byte `0xe0` yields `level = 3`, raw `windowBits = 8`, `memLevel = 9`, and `strategy = 4`; the `level == 0 || level == 1` normalization does not fire.

The raw `windowBits = 8` from step 4 is promoted to 9, so `s->w_size` and the `s->prev` table are 512 entries wide. `s->prev` is allocated through `ZALLOC`; on this platform `zcalloc()` uses `malloc(items * size)`, so the buffer starts uninitialized.

The attacker-derived compression choices are copied into persistent deflate state. For this witness, the state now carries `s->level = 3` and `s->strategy = 4` (`Z_FIXED`), which later drive the algorithm dispatch in `deflate()`.
Resetting the deflate state clears `head[]` only. The macro comment says `prev[] will be initialized on the fly`, so untouched `s->prev` slots retain the malloc-backed garbage from step 5.

Initialization derives the level-dependent compression limits from `configuration_table[s->level]`. With `s->level = 3`, `configuration_table[3].max_lazy` is `6`; `deflate_state` aliases `max_insert_length` to `max_lazy_match`, so later `deflate_fast()` compares `s->match_length` against `6`.

The helper passes the same witness buffer and the clamped `dictionaryLen` into zlib as a preset dictionary. For this run, `deflateSetDictionary()` receives `data` and `224`, so only the first 224 bytes are preloaded before normal compression.

fine_trace.var: s->lookahead, str, n, s->prev[str & s->w_mask], s->head[s->ins_h]
fine_trace.note: The preset-dictionary load fills the window with 224 bytes, and this loop inserts only the positions it can hash from that dictionary: `str = 0..221`. Slots outside that inserted prefix remain untouched.

Dictionary preload ends with `s->strstart = 224`, `s->insert = 2`, and `s->lookahead = 0`. The next fill therefore has exactly two carry-over positions left to initialize before real compression continues.

Actual compression now runs on the full 538-byte witness while the partially initialized state from step 11 stays live. The same buffer is reused as the deflate payload, and `c_stream.avail_in = 538` makes real input available to the later `fill_window()` calls.

fine_trace.code:
bstate = s->level == 0 ? deflate_stored(s, flush) :
         s->strategy == Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY ? deflate_huff(s, flush) :
         s->strategy == Z_RLE ? deflate_rle(s, flush) :
         (*(configuration_table[s->level].func))(s, flush);
fine_trace.note: Because the caller supplied input, `deflate()` evaluates this dispatch. With `s->level = 3` and `s->strategy = 4` (`Z_FIXED`), the first three arms are false and `configuration_table[3].func` selects `deflate_fast`.

fine_trace.var: s->lookahead, s->insert, str, s->prev[str & s->w_mask], s->head[s->ins_h]
fine_trace.note: The first `fill_window()` during real compression consumes the carry-over state from step 11. With `s->strstart = 224` and `s->insert = 2`, it starts at `str = 222` and writes exactly the two leftover dictionary positions `222` and `223`, extending the initialized prefix from step 10's `0..221` to `0..223` before normal compression resumes.

From the state created in step 8, this predicate treats matches longer than `6` as too large to backfill. When that happens, the `else` arm advances `s->strstart` without `INSERT_STRING` on the skipped positions, so positions after the initialized `0..223` range can remain untouched. The observed uninitialized read implies this branch was taken on at least one later match, though the saved artifacts do not expose which one.

The slide threshold is reached on the witnessed input. Step 11 started real compression at `strstart = 224`, step 12 provided `dataLen = 538`, and step 5 made `wsize = 512`; with `MAX_DIST(s) = wsize - MIN_LOOKAHEAD = 250`, consuming the full payload lets `s->strstart` reach `224 + 538 = 762`, so `fill_window()` eventually takes this branch and calls `slide_hash(s)`.

Root cause. `slide_hash()` iterates backward across all `wsize` `prev[]` slots. After step 14 initialized only positions `0..223` from the dictionary path and step 15 skipped at least one later insertion, some later modulo-512 slot still contains the malloc-backed garbage from step 5, so this load pulls that uninitialized value into local `m`.

Sink. The ternary compares the uninitialized `m` from step 17 against `wsize` and then stores a value derived from it back through `*p`. Stage 01's saved report is `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/zlib/deflate.c:222:20`.

allocation_context.note: The saved origin stack points to `s->prev = (Posf *) ZALLOC(...)`; `ZALLOC` ultimately reaches malloc-backed `zcalloc()` on this platform.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved command `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_49903 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` ran `/out/example_dict_fuzzer` on `poc` and reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `slide_hash`.

format.name: example_dict_fuzzer input buffer reused as preset dictionary and deflate payload
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 538-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_49903/poc` (sha256 `386e8e62c47580703ab0972569c39baa2b587c0edf64743ff5ed6c79c89ce87a`). In this witness, byte 0 is `0xe0`, so `test_dict_deflate()` derives `level = 3`, raw `windowBits = 8`, `memLevel = 9`, and `strategy = 4`, while the caller also sets `dictionaryLen = 224`. zlib promotes `windowBits` to 9, stores `level` / `strategy` in `s`, and `lm_init()` derives `max_insert_length == 6` from `configuration_table[3]`. The same witness is then used both as the 224-byte preset dictionary and as the 538-byte deflate payload: dictionary insertion covers positions `0..221`, the first real `fill_window()` covers carry-over positions `222` and `223`, and the remaining trigger requires at least one later `deflate_fast()` long-match skip before `strstart` reaches `224 + 538 = 762`, the `wsize + MAX_DIST(s)` threshold that calls `slide_hash()`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader claim about other first-byte values, other lengths, or other input families.
